answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it earns voting weight or reputation. A single attacker can still create many keys, but must fund every lock and cannot reuse that capital elsewhere until release; slashing deposits tied to provable double-signing raises the risk further. The tundra of dormant accounts, a zephyr of fresh keys, or a violet profile does not evade the same per-identity bond, so scaling a sybil attack becomes costly rather than free.
